events.label: Proterozoic, geography unknown
events.description: A dim land/sea noise field captioned "geography unknown" — no plate reconstruction covers this span. It closes the gap between the end of Archean-haze coverage and the 1 Ga start of the Merdith et al. 2021 plate model, which is what makes true reconstructed continents possible again from 1000 Ma onward (docs/GLOBE.md §4.1).
events.citation: Merdith, A.S. et al. (2021). "Extending full-plate tectonic models into deep time: Linking the Neoproterozoic and the Phanerozoic." Earth-Science Reviews, 214, 103477 (model coverage begins at 1000 Ma). Gumsley, A.P. et al. (2017). PNAS, 114(8), 1811-1816 (Great Oxidation Event onset, ~2.4 Ga, bounds this regime's older edge).

events.label: Paleoproterozoic glaciation
events.description: The first Paleoproterozoic global glaciation, dated by the Ongeluk Formation (South Africa) and correlated units. Onset is dated to 2.46-2.426 Ga; global extent (a true "Snowball Earth" versus a regional ice age) is contested, unlike the better-constrained Cryogenian glaciations. Rendered with the same ice-shell effect as Snowball Earth (docs/GLOBE.md §4.3), captioned "extent contested".
events.citation: Gumsley, A.P. et al. (2017). "Timing and tempo of the Great Oxidation Event." PNAS, 114(8), 1811-1816 ("first Paleoproterozoic global glaciation").

events.label: Archean haze, scattered protocrust
events.description: An anoxic ocean world with small scattered flecks of protocrust at procedural positions (no plate reconstruction exists this far back). The atmosphere stays anoxic until the Great Oxidation Event (onset 2.46-2.43 Ga). An orange-tan organic haze has been proposed for episodes of the Neoarchean; this is contested and shown only as an occasional tint, not a permanent state.
events.citation: Lyons, T.W., Reinhard, C.T. & Planavsky, N.J. (2014). "The rise of oxygen in Earth's early ocean and atmosphere." Nature, 506, 307-315. Zerkle, A.L. et al. (2012). "A bistable organic-rich atmosphere on the Neoarchaean Earth." Nature Geoscience, 5, 359-363 (haze episodes, contested).

events.label: Hadean water world
events.description: A global ocean under a steam-veiled atmosphere, no continents yet drawn. Detrital zircons from the Jack Hills, Australia, are the earliest evidence for continental crust and liquid-water oceans, dated to 4.4 Gyr ago — this regime's upper (older) bound is therefore a "by this date" bound, not a moment of origin.
events.citation: Wilde, S.A., Valley, J.W., Peck, W.H. & Graham, C.M. (2001). "Evidence from detrital zircons for the existence of continental crust and oceans on the Earth 4.4 Gyr ago." Nature, 409, 175-178.

events.label: Magma ocean and newborn Moon
events.description: The freshly accreted Earth, its surface a crust of cooling magma cracked by heat from the Moon-forming impact, with the newly formed Moon still close and large in the sky. Same contested date range as the `moon-forming-impact` event in events-core: Hf-W and zircon U-Pb dating place the impact at 4.51-4.52 Ga, while a 2024 tidal-remelting model argues the lunar rock record instead reflects a later heating event around 4.35 Ga.
events.citation: Barboni, M. et al. (2017). "Early formation of the Moon 4.51 billion years ago." Science Advances, 3, e1602365. Thiemens, M.M. et al. (2019). "Early Moon formation inferred from hafnium-tungsten systematics." Nature Geoscience, 12, 696-700. Contested by: Nimmo, F., Kleine, T. & Morbidelli, A. (2024). "Tidally driven remelting around 4.35 billion years ago indicates the Moon is old." Nature, 636, 598-602.
